newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Salomon says YPF share sale a success.
newsitem.headline: Salomon says YPF share sale a success.

text.p: Salomon Brothers announced the sale Wednesday of virtually all the 10 percent of shares in Argentine oil firm YPF in employees' hands for almost $1.0 billion.
About 96 percent of YPF staff shares were sucessfully placed at $29.25 each, said Salomon in a press release.
The shares sold were owned by YPF employees under a Shared Property Program launched after the company's privatization in 1993.
A total of 33.79 million shares were sold, Salomon said.
Net proceeds from the sale include $585 million that will be chanelled to cancel debts of YPF employees with the Argentine state. YPF will get no money from the deal.
The shares were sold to institutional investors in the United States (70 percent), Europe (15 percent) and Argentina (15 percent), Salomon said.
Banco Comafi and Merchant Bankers Asociados, an Argentine affiliate of Salomon, as well as U.S. Vestrust Securities LP, also acted as underwriters.
The sale received a green light late Tuesday when an Argentine judge modified an earlier ruling after YPF made a deposit of $400,000 in guarantees.
Judge Enrique Arias Gibert had Monday ordered the suspension of the sale following a complaint by 11 former YPF workers that claim they were left out from the program.
Judicial sources said many other former YPF employees may make similar claims in other courts.

Argentina's government authorized the sale of the Class C YPF shares in the hands of the company's employees by a decree issued last Friday. The shares are to be auctioned simultaneously in New York and Buenos Aires.
The government owns another 20 percent of the firm but says it has no immediate plans to sell.
